Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

for the final section record the discussion plan as it stands now after the film we will leave ten minutes for questions and then ask people to write comments on index cards the cards go in the blue envelope in the society cabinet and are not to be photographed with names visible we do not yet know whether the director can join by video so do not list her as a guest in the announcement if she is unavailable priya can read the two questions sent by members last month and we can end by telling people when the next wednesday meeting is the next meeting is november sixth at five thirty in the old library seminar room and that is the last item for these notes", "output": "So this is the update for the North Vale College Film Society and our screening plan for the last week of October. We meet every Wednesday in the Old Library seminar room, and we have twenty-three active members this term. The society is run by students, but the media office holds the equipment account, and the student union has to confirm rooms for public events. I am dictating this after our meeting on October 9, and I want the notes to include what is settled and what is still waiting on someone else.

Our main screening is meant to be on Friday, October 25, in the East Hall lecture room. We first put West Hall in the draft—no, East Hall is the room that the union offered, and that has the wider doorway for the portable screen. The room seats 112, and we are keeping thirty chairs free along the side for people who need more space. The event is open to students and staff, but we have not advertised it as open to the public because the building closes to visitors at 9:30.

We are considering The Silent Harbor, a 1998 documentary about a family-run ferry service, and the film is eighty-four minutes long. The director is Lena Mori, and the society watched the library copy at our September meeting. After that screening, two members asked whether we could show it with captions because the archive file has captions for the dialogue but not for the short section of harbor announcements. I have emailed the archive about that section, and they have not replied yet, so the caption question is still open.

At the meeting, Maya asked if setup starts at six, and I said, “Right, six is when the media office lets us collect the projector, not when the room opens.” We can enter East Hall at 6:15 because a chemistry class uses it until six. The society has borrowed a folding screen from the language department and two powered speakers from the radio club. The projector stays with the media office and must be returned to the locked cabinet by 9:45. Joel is the member with the cabinet code, but he will be in lab until 6:30, so we should not plan the equipment check before he arrives.

The secretary asked me to dictate three things we need to follow up on:
1. Priya will ask the archive by Monday whether the harbor announcements have a separate caption file and whether we may use it for this single campus screening.
2. Noah will check with the media office about an extra HDMI cable because the society cable worked only when the connector was held at an angle at the September showing.
3. I will ask the union whether the thirty side chairs can stay in place during the whole event or have to be stacked before the lecture room is locked.
These are tasks and not confirmations.

We also talked about a possible second film. If the archive cannot provide captions for the announcements by Tuesday evening, we will move to Borrowed Skies, which is a seventy-one-minute campus-made film with captions already embedded. The condition matters because the student director has said the film may be shown only if we tell her the final choice by Wednesday at noon. She has not given permission for any later date, and nobody at the meeting treated the backup as chosen. If the caption file arrives on time, we will stay with The Silent Harbor. If it does not arrive, we need to contact the director before we change the listing.

There is a small language detail in the draft introduction that came up because two exchange students are helping host the night. Felix said in German, “Er bringt die Kabel um acht,” meaning he is bringing the cables at eight, and he meant that he would carry them to the hall, not that he was uncertain about it. Ines replied in casual Portuguese, “Beleza,” when I asked if she could read the welcome note, and she meant okay, she can do it. I am leaving both remarks in the notes because they were answers to practical questions and not hesitation from the speakers.

The welcome note will name the director and give the film length before the screening. Felix can read the first paragraph in German if he has finished the sign-in list by 6:40, and Ines will read the English introduction after him. She prefers not to be photographed while reading, so the publicity volunteer should get a wide room picture before the lights go down. The volunteer has permission to photograph the audience area but not to record the film or the discussion, and that limit was repeated at the meeting.

We have thirty-six dollars remaining in the society event budget after buying two rolls of paper tape and printing the draft posters. The union can reimburse up to twelve dollars for accessible seating signs, but the treasurer has not submitted the form yet. The posters are in a folder on TideBoard and still say West Hall because the room change was made after they were drafted. I have not asked anyone to print them. The secretary will update the location after the union confirms the room in writing, and the final version needs to keep the start time at seven.

For the final section, record the discussion plan as it stands now. After the film, we will leave ten minutes for questions and then ask people to write comments on index cards. The cards go in the blue envelope in the society cabinet and are not to be photographed with names visible. We do not yet know whether the director can join by video, so do not list her as a guest in the announcement. If she is unavailable, Priya can read the two questions sent by members last month, and we can end by telling people when the next Wednesday meeting is. The next meeting is November 6 at 5:30 in the Old Library seminar room, and that is the last item for these notes."}]
